messages:
Morgan: Quick sync — I want to reduce inference-worker StatefulSet from 8 -> 3 today to cut costs. Before I push the TF change, couple of checks: PVC behavior (will we orphan volumes?), rollout approach (partitioned vs full rolling), and any secret/mount weirdness. Anyone seen problems with this pattern recently?

Jasper: scaling STS down will terminate pods with ordinals >= newReplicaCount. PVCs created from volumeClaimTemplates are NOT deleted automatically — they stick around (you can end up with orphaned PVCs/PVs if you don't clean them). PV reclaimPolicy controls PV after PVC deletion, not automatic here.

Jasper: My recommendation: 1) use a partitioned rolling update so we can control which ordinals are torn down, 2) run a pre-check script to list PVCs that match the statefulset name, 3) ensure our app handles SIGTERM cleanly (drain/flush).

Anya: Terraform note — we manage the STS via k8s_manifest in infra-main. Change looks like:

```hcl
resource "kubernetes_manifest" "inference_worker_sts" {
  manifest = yamldecode(file("manifests/inference-worker-sts.yaml"))
  // update replicas in the manifest file and apply plan
}
```

Anya: Alternatively we can patch the running STS first to the partitioned update and then update the manifest so the TF plan is a noop after. Reduces blast radius.

Linh: Also check podManagementPolicy — default is OrderedReady which is safer for stateful workloads. If you change to Parallel for faster termination you might get data races with PVCs. I'd keep OrderedReady for this.

Linh: Add a preStop hook so pods have a small buffer before SIGKILL. Example: 

```yaml
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 25"]
```

(Assumes app flushes on SIGTERM)

Jasper: For the partitioned patch (apply before TF change):

```bash
kubectl patch statefulset inference-worker -n prod --type='merge' -p '{"spec": {"updateStrategy": {"type": "RollingUpdate", "rollingUpdate": {"partition": 3}}}}'
```

Jasper: That keeps ordinals 0..2 running and will only terminate 3..7. Then we can watch the terminated pods, cleanup PVCs if desired, and finally set replicas in TF to 3.

SRE-bot: Preflight PVC check I can run: lists PVCs tied to the sts and their PV status:

```bash
kubectl get pvc -n prod -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.phase} {.spec.volumeName}\n' | grep inference-worker || true
```

SRE-bot: I can also run a dry-run TF plan in the validation workspace and post the plan link here.

Morgan: Perfect. Two quick Qs: 1) If we scale down then later scale back up, will the existing PVCs be reused automatically? 2) Who will apply the patch/TF change?

Jasper: 1) If PVCs remain (untouched) and pods come back with the same ordinal, they will reattach the existing PVCs. If you manually delete PVCs, then new empty PVCs/PVs will be provisioned.

Jasper: 2) I can: I'll 1) apply the partition patch, 2) run SRE-bot PVC check, 3) update manifests + open a TF plan PR. I'll wait 15m for objections before starting.

Anya: One more gotcha — secrets mounted from projected volumes are fine, but if you've been using subPath mounts with secrets and the container image expects files to exist at startup, restarting with fewer replicas might surface timing issues. Quick grep in manifests for "subPath" is worth doing.

Linh: I'll review the preStop + readinessProbe to make sure probes give pods time to terminate gracefully.

Morgan: Thanks all — no objections here. Jasper, ping when you start. :thumbsup:

Jasper: Starting in ~10m. Will post the patch cmd + TF plan link when ready.

SRE-bot: Dry-run TF plan scheduled: https://ci.internal/redwood/tf-plan/12345 (read-only)

Morgan: :rocket:
